checks.source_as_cited: Cochrane Handbook; PRISMA-P 2015; PRISMA 2020; PRISMA-S 2021; GRADE 2008; GRADE EtD 2016; Garritty et al. 2021
checks.note: Bibliographic records checked: PRISMA-P (Moher 2015, Syst Rev), PRISMA 2020 (Page 2021, BMJ), PRISMA-S (Rethlefsen 2021, Syst Rev), GRADE (Guyatt 2008, BMJ), EtD (Alonso-Coello 2016, BMJ) are right from standard records. Rapid-review paper confirmed by PubMed record: Garritty, Gartlehner, Nussbaumer-Streit, King, Hamel, Kamel, Affengruber, Stevens, 'Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group offers evidence-informed guidance to conduct rapid reviews', J Clin Epidemiol 2021;130:13-22. It is the interim guidance; an updated version was published later. These sources describe the review process and its reporting; the stage-by-stage mapping onto the design and the claim that it targets those faults is the design's own analogy, not stated by the sources. GRADE is built for rating evidence on health outcomes.
checks.correction: Garritty et al. 2021 is the interim guidance (vol 130, pp 13-22); the guidance was later updated.

checks.note: Well-known; textbook description. Majority accuracy tends to 1 with independent voters each with p>0.5. Same theorem also gives the converse (tends to 0 if p<0.5). Used standard knowledge/survey descriptions.

Real paper (AJPS 36(3):617-634). It gives conditions on the average correlation (bounded relative to competence) under which majority still beats an individual. Whether the correlation must be known is the design's gloss; the gain shrinking with correlation is right in spirit, but with positive correlation the limit need not reach 1. Based on standard description of the result.
checks.correction: The guarantee is a condition on average pairwise correlation (bounded relative to competence), not a gain for any bounded correlation.

checks.note: E = mean member error minus ambiguity, for squared loss with a weighted-average ensemble; ambiguity is nonnegative so the ensemble is never worse than the mean member. Recalled from the standard record; not re-fetched.

Real paper (Machine Learning 51:181-207). It defines and compares pairwise and non-pairwise diversity measures on labelled data. Its own conclusion is that no clear, consistent relationship between the measures and ensemble accuracy was found, so it supports computing diversity but not using it as a guarantee. Based on abstract as remembered from standard record.
checks.correction: Add that the paper found no reliable link between the diversity measures and accuracy.

checks.source_as_cited: Seung, Opper, Sompolinsky 1992 Query by committee, COLT
checks.note: Real (COLT 1992, pp 287-294). The result is for a specific setting (perceptron-type learners, committee sampled from the version space), where querying points of committee disagreement gives information gain bounded below and error falling exponentially in the number of queries. 'Carry the most information' is a fair summary only in that setting.
checks.correction: Guarantee is shown for sampling from the version space in the original setting; not general disagreement.

checks.note: Standard textbook (Wiley). Design effect for clusters is 1+(m-1)rho; n_eff = n/deff. The equal-correlation approximation is the book's own.

Real paper (Appl Stat 28(1):20-28). EM gives maximum-likelihood error rates and class posteriors without a gold standard, under conditional independence of raters given the true class. It converges only to a local maximum and needs enough raters per item for identifiability; 'recovers' is a consistency claim under the model being right.
checks.correction: Local optimum, identifiability needs enough raters/items; guarantee holds only if the independence model is correct.

checks.note: Real (Biometrics 36:167-171). Two tests in two populations with different prevalence and the same Se/Sp gives identifiability, assuming conditional independence. Standard description.

Real (Biometrics 41:959-968). Positive conditional dependence biases estimates when independence is assumed (prevalence and accuracy overestimated in the usual case). 'Both tests look more accurate' is the standard reading for positive dependence.

checks.source_as_cited: Rogan and Gladen 1978 Am J Epidemiol
checks.note: Real (AJE 107:71-76). True prevalence = (observed + Sp - 1)/(Se + Sp - 1). Unbiased with known Se, Sp; uncertainty in them is not propagated by the point estimate, and the result can fall outside [0,1].
Real (Biometrics 39:207-215). Correction under verification depending only on observed test result and covariates (missing at random).

checks.source_as_cited: Cohen 1960; Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990 J Clin Epidemiol
checks.note: Cohen 1960, Educ Psychol Meas 20:37-46; Feinstein and Cicchetti, J Clin Epidemiol 43(6):543-549, part I on the two paradoxes (high agreement with low kappa, and effect of marginal asymmetry). Standard records.

Real (Bell Syst Tech J 8(4):613-631). Single-sampling plans with lot tolerance percent defective and average outgoing quality limit under rectifying inspection. Risks are bounded per plan at the stated defect rates, not for any lot.

Real (16:117-186). SPRT controls error rates alpha and beta approximately (via Wald's bounds). That it needs the fewest items on average among all tests with those error rates was proved by Wald and Wolfowitz (1948), not in the 1945 paper; it is for simple hypotheses.
checks.correction: Optimality proof is Wald and Wolfowitz 1948 (Ann Math Stat 19:326-339).

checks.source_as_cited: Clopper and Pearson 1934; Hanley and Lippman-Hand 1983
checks.note: Biometrika 26:404-413 and JAMA 249:1743-1745. Exact limits are conservative (coverage at least nominal). Rule of three: 3/n at 95% one-sided.
Lincoln 1930 is USDA Circular 118. Estimator N = n1*n2/m. Assumptions listed are the standard ones. Standard textbook record.
Real (vol 1, pp 131-160). N = (n1+1)(n2+1)/(m+1) - 1 is defined at m=0 and is exactly unbiased only when n1+n2 >= N; with small overlap (small samples) a bias remains.
checks.correction: Nearly unbiased when n1+n2 is at least about N, not for small overlap in general.

checks.note: Real (Biometrika 59:591-603). Log-linear models for incomplete 2^k tables; dependences are identified only up to the assumption that the highest-order interaction is zero, and the zero cell is unobserved.

Real (BMJ 313:342-343, short paper). It applies capture-recapture to literature searches; its own point is that the assumptions (independence, equal catchability) are usually violated, so the estimate is rough. Based on standard record.
Real (15:657-680). TOST is level-alpha for the equivalence margin. 'Replicate observations' is loosely stated; the test is a normal-theory test on a mean difference.
Real (12:153-157). Only discordant pairs count; pairs must be independent.
Real (22(11):1359-1366). Simulations and examples show flexibility can push false positives above 60 percent.
BMJ 311:485. Statistics note; recommends confidence intervals.
Real (8(4):355-362). TOST against smallest effect size of interest.

Real (Syst Rev 4:1). PRISMA-P is a reporting checklist for protocols; it does not itself register or freeze a protocol (registries such as PROSPERO do that), and does not enforce reporting against it.
checks.correction: Registration is done through a registry; PRISMA-P specifies what to report.

checks.note: Real (Syst Rev 10:39). 16-item checklist for reporting searches.
Real (BMJ 372:n71). Flow diagram and an item on excluded studies with reasons.

checks.source_as_cited: Buscemi et al. 2006 J Clin Epidemiol
checks.note: Real (59:697-703). Small randomized comparison of 30 trials in paediatric reviews; found single extraction produced more errors (about 21.7 vs 13.0 percent). 'Independent humans' is the study's setup; whether it transfers to non-human extractors is not tested.
BMJ 336:924-926. Four levels of certainty with stated downgrade domains. Ratings still involve judgment, so repeatability is not guaranteed.

checks.source_as_cited: Lundh et al. 2017 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
checks.note: Real (MR000033, 'Industry sponsorship and research outcome'). Sponsored studies found more favourable efficacy results and conclusions. Claimed caveat about drugs and devices is right.
BMJ 315:629-634. Funnel-plot asymmetry regression test; the ten-study threshold is from later guidance (Sterne 2011), not this paper.
Real book, 'Experts in Uncertainty: Opinion and Subjective Probability in Science'. Classical model weights on calibration and information from seed variables.
Real (Wiley), full title as cited. G-study estimates variance components; D-study projects dependability for other designs.
Real (41:100-115). CUSUM has a known ARL to false alarm, computed under a known in-control distribution and independent observations. Optimality (Moustakides 1986) is a later result.

Confirmed by search record: SIGIR 2016, DOI 10.1145/2911451.2911510. The target method gives a probabilistic reliability guarantee (95 percent at 70 percent recall); the knee method does not, it is a heuristic with good empirical reliability. The claim attributes a guarantee to both.
checks.correction: Guarantee belongs to the target method only; the knee method is empirical, with no probabilistic guarantee.

checks.note: Same caveats as D6-04: the independence and equal catchability assumptions are weakly met for ranked search.

Real (9:65-72). Internal pilot re-estimates sample size from the nuisance variance. Later work (Kieser and Friede; Gould) shows type I error is controlled approximately and is blinded-variance dependent; 'without biasing' holds only under the usual conditions.

result.overall: All 40 citations resolve to real works with correct titles, authors, years and venues. I confirmed two (Garritty 2021 and Cormack and Grossman 2016) by search; the rest by well-established bibliographic records recalled from memory, not re-fetched. Substantive caveats: Cormack and Grossman's guarantee belongs to the target method, not the knee method. Wald 1945 does not contain the optimality proof, which is Wald and Wolfowitz 1948. Chapman is near-unbiased only when n1+n2 is at least about N. Kuncheva and Whitaker found no reliable diversity-accuracy link. PRISMA-P is a reporting guide, not a registry. Ladha's result needs a bound on average correlation. Garritty 2021 is the interim guidance.
